overview: This bill sets aside new protected areas in the Shawnee National Forest in southern Illinois. It designates about 750 acres as the Camp Hutchins Wilderness, the strictest level of federal land protection, and closes a forest road there to cars so it can serve as a hiking trail. It also creates three Special Management Areas covering roughly 12,700 acres (Camp Hutchins, Ripple Hollow and Burke Branch) to be managed for conservation, biodiversity, research and public recreation. In those areas, commercial logging, trapping and most motor vehicle use would be banned, while hunting, prescribed burns, invasive species control and restoration work would continue, and all of the protected land would be closed to new mining and drilling claims. The Forest Service would have to write a management plan within three years. As of October 27, 2025, the bill had been approved by a Senate committee and placed on the Senate's calendar.
for: Supporters say the bill protects some of Illinois' most ecologically valuable forest land for good while keeping hunting, hiking and active restoration work such as controlled burns.
against: Critics say the new restrictions on logging, vehicles, trapping and mining limit how local residents and businesses can use the forest, and that the bill orders roads closed and land purchased without spelling out the costs.
